title: Road Position, Parking, Pedestrians, and Accident Response

location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Drivers should use the correct side of the road, signal and maneuver carefully, avoid obstructing traffic, respect pedestrians and cyclists, and respond responsibly after accidents.
content.cultural_context: Kejati Bali's foreigner legal FAQ summarizes left-side driving, signaling before turns, avoiding mobile phone use, and respecting pedestrian and traffic rules. The 2025 Governor Circular requires compliance with Indonesian traffic regulations and signs.
content.significance: Predictable driving and consideration for vulnerable road users reduce conflict, especially on narrow or crowded roads.
common_situations: Joining traffic from a side road
Being involved in a road accident

do: Signal before turning or changing direction
Park only where permitted and do not block traffic or pedestrian paths
If an accident occurs, stop, assist where safe, and contact police or emergency services when required
dont: Leave an accident scene without following legal duties

common_misconceptions: Road etiquette is also about predictable behavior and consideration, not only avoiding fines.
regional_variations: Road layouts and parking controls differ by locality; follow signs, markings, and police directions.
content.additional_notes: The Kejati FAQ is explanatory information, not a substitute for current statutory text. Accident procedures need direct current legal/police confirmation.

sources.title: Foreigner Legal Service — Traffic Law FAQ
Bali Governor Circular Letter No. 07 of 2025 on Foreign Tourist Conduct
Bali Police Urge Vehicle Rental Companies to Educate Foreign Tourists on Traffic Rules

verification.verification_notes: Left-side driving and basic road conduct are supported; detailed accident procedures need a direct current statutory or police source.

sensitivity.handling_notes: Use neutral, precise wording; distinguish formal rules from courtesy recommendations.
